# Skribli

Skribli is a local-first contextual annotation application for Windows 10 and Windows 11. Public downloads are disabled, while the encrypted owner v0 installer is available through a key-protected page. The current release supports pastel typed and handwritten Skribs, pen/highlighter/eraser input, local image/video/document attachments, one-time reminders, and a local calendar.

## Current workflow

- Focus a supported Windows application.
- Press Ctrl + Shift + Space.
- Skribli clears any previous target and revalidates the foreground window and process identity.
- With no matching active note, Skribli creates one empty note.
- With an existing active match, Skribli reopens the deterministic existing note.
- Type, draw, attach a local reference, or set a reminder in one focused paper-like editor.
- Done, Escape, Ctrl+Enter, or close waits for text and rich content to save, then folds the active note into a movable pastel dot.
- Select or move the dot to reopen or reposition the active note. The current v0 shows one active note or dot at a time.
- Ordinary Delete moves a saved note to local Trash. An untouched empty note uses a separate constrained discard path.
- The background process remains available in the Windows system tray.

## All Skribs

All Skribs is a normal, non-floating, taskbar-visible library opened from the tray. It provides:

- separate searchable Notes and Trash views;
- same-record restore and separately confirmed permanent deletion;
- selected/all-record schema-version-2 JSON export with explicit rich-content exclusions;
- import compatibility for legacy schema-version-1 note-record exports;
- local-only portable JSON import with mandatory native preview;
- exact duplicate detection and stable-ID conflict handling;
- revision-locked apply and a durably verified pre-import rollback backup;
- read and export access when writes are blocked.

Imported files are not uploaded and never cause Skribli to launch, focus, guess, or re-anchor an external application.

## Implemented foundations

- fail-closed foreground target capture;
- deterministic native create-versus-reopen requests;
- ordered local note saves with truthful state and retry behavior;
- schema-v3 crash-safe local storage with schema-v1/v2 migration and recovery generations;
- reversible 30-day Trash without silent automatic purge;
- truthful local note-record export and portable JSON import with preview and rollback;
- editable vector drawing, bounded local attachments, reminders, and calendar views;
- saved-note collapse/restore through one movable pastel dot;
- target-monitor work-area placement;
- bounded Windows accessibility-event delivery;
- single-instance routing;
- first-run guidance and a reopenable tray Quick guide.

## Not in the current MVP

The current build does not ship multiple simultaneous note windows/dots, attached tabs, screenshot pins, checklists, cloud sync, a permanent toolbar, or a full-screen selective click-through overlay.

## Availability

- Platform under active validation: Windows 10 and Windows 11, x64
- Public downloads: disabled
- Owner v0 installer: available through the encrypted key-protected page
- macOS: not available
- Website: https://skribly-desktop.vercel.app/
- Development notes: https://skribly-desktop.vercel.app/release-notes
- Privacy policy: https://skribly-desktop.vercel.app/privacy
- FAQ: https://skribly-desktop.vercel.app/answers

## Open release gates

Public installer access remains disabled until the exact Windows release candidate completes rich-content portability decisions, optional scheduled/user-selected backups, automatic/configurable retention decisions, installer upgrade/repair/uninstall checks, accessibility and long-session physical testing, compatibility documentation, trusted code signing, support readiness, and final delivery reconciliation.

## Privacy

A verified account is required for trial and write access. The account service stores verified email, entitlement dates, a one-way device claim, app version, and optional product-update consent. Skrib content remains local and is not uploaded. Skribli reads limited Windows process, window identity, and geometry information locally when validating a shortcut target. Export and import operate on user-selected local JSON files. The public website currently adds no advertising cookies or behavioural analytics.
